title: Rare and Endangered Fish Species in The Adriatic Sea and Proposal for Marine Flagship Species
reference: Pešić, A., Ikica, Z., Joksimović, A., Djurović, M., Laušević, R. (2018): Rare and Endangered Fish Species in The Adriatic Sea and Proposal for Marine Flagship Species. Kotor: University of Montenegro, Institute of Marine Biology. 36 pp.
authors: Pešić, A., Ikica, Z., Joksimović, A., Djurović, M., Laušević, R.
publisher: Kotor: University of Montenegro, Institute of Marine Biology
description:
This study and publication were carried out under the project “Marine Biodiversity Conservation Center “Boka Aquarium” (MonteAqua)”, implemented by the Institute of Marine Biology of the University of Montenegro (IMB) in cooperation with the Center for Fisheries and Biodiversity Conservation of Inland Waters, Institute of Biology and Ecology, Faculty of Science, University of Kragujevac. Study is developed as IMB’s project co-funding.

Summary

Adriatic fish diversity remains incompletely documented, particularly in the southern basin below 500 m, with some historical records unreliable and new species recorded annually. The reviewed assessments identify numerous threatened species, including 15 Critically Endangered and 15 Endangered species, while European sturgeon (Acipenser sturio) is classified as regionally extinct in the Adriatic.

Fishing, by-catch, habitat degradation, pollution, invasive species and climate change are major pressures. Conservation measures include fishing restrictions, seasonal and spatial closures, and marine protected areas.

The text also highlights flagship species as tools for public awareness and conservation fundraising. John Dory (Zeus faber) was selected as Aquarium Boka’s flagship species through stakeholder consultation, reflecting its distinctive appearance, local importance and high commercial value.

The study reports 449 fish species and subspecies in the Adriatic, while noting unreliable historical records and substantial gaps in knowledge, particularly below 500 m in the southern basin. The reviewed assessments identify 15 Critically Endangered and 15 Endangered species, with European sturgeon (Acipenser sturio) classified as regionally extinct in the Adriatic.

Overfishing and by-catch are major threats, compounded by habitat degradation, pollution, invasive species and climate change. Conservation priorities include further research, fishing restrictions and ecosystem protection through marine protected areas.

Stakeholder consultation selected John Dory (Zeus faber) as Aquarium Boka’s flagship species, recognising its distinctive appearance and local economic importance as assets for raising public awareness and supporting marine biodiversity conservation.
